nodes.label: .agents/skills/ skills directory
nodes.rationale: Holds installed and local skills in one place; .claude/skills/ symlinks to it instead of keeping a copy.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md (agent instruction entry point)
nodes.rationale: Entry point for every agent harness. It states what the repository builds (Layerhand, an agent that retouches photographs inside a real image editor and returns a layered file, for the OpenAI x Product Hunt GPT-6 Astra Challenge) and @-imports eleven documents in three groups, each with a note on what it covers: instructions (Andrej Karpathy skills, graphify, RTK, project conventions, skills), references (git workflow, Markdown style guide) and project documents (PRODUCT, PRD, TRD, Product Hunt ideas). Harnesses without import support open the files directly. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are symlinks to it, so edits go to AGENTS.md only.

nodes.label: Skills (installed skill collections)
nodes.rationale: Skills are packaged instructions an agent loads when a task calls for them. They live in .agents/skills/, which .claude/skills/ symlinks to; all but one come from three external collections, and astra-challenge, which ran the ideation, was written in this repository.

Its caveat that AGENTS.md does not import rules.md is out of date: the current AGENTS.md imports docs/agents/rules.md. Outcome: useful.

nodes.label: Saved query: what connects @commitlint/cli, @commitlint/config-conventional and husky
nodes.norm_label: saved query: what connects @commitlint/cli, @commitlint/config-conventional and husky
nodes.rationale: Answer: not a documentation gap. graphify's AST pass emits two nodes for each package.json devDependency (the dependency key and an import reference), and usually only one of each pair carries edges; the @commitlint/cli import reference links to the three workflow jobs that run commitlint. The files that actually use husky, commitlint and lint-staged are the extensionless hook scripts in .husky/ (commit-msg, pre-commit, pre-push), which graphify never scanned, so those edges were missing. Outcome: useful.

nodes.label: .husky/pre-push hook
nodes.rationale: Blocks a push straight to the default branch, so work reaches main only through a pull request. Like every local hook it is fast feedback that --no-verify can skip.

nodes.label: bun (package manager and script runner)
nodes.rationale: bun, not npm or yarn: bun install and bun run lint are the project entry points.

nodes.label: graphify-labs/graphify skill collection
nodes.rationale: Builds a knowledge graph of the repository in graphify-out/ and answers questions from it, so agents read a scoped subgraph instead of raw files.

nodes.label: Prettier owns syntax, not prose
nodes.rationale: bun run lint checks the whole tree and lint-staged fixes staged files on commit, so do not hand-format around it. printWidth applies to code and proseWrap is left at preserve, so Prettier never rewraps a Markdown paragraph: the 80-character limit is the author's to keep and nothing checks it.

nodes.label: Local hook setup (bun install, then uv tool install graphifyy)
nodes.norm_label: local hook setup (bun install, then uv tool install graphifyy)
nodes.rationale: bun install installs the local hooks, but the pre-commit hook also runs graphify to update the knowledge graph and bun install does not provide it, so graphify is installed first with uv tool install graphifyy or every commit fails.

nodes.rationale: Blocks a commit whose message is not conventional, using the same commitlint rule set as the workflows.

nodes.label: Conventional commit types (build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test)
nodes.norm_label: conventional commit types (build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test)

nodes.label: Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Used for commit subjects, issue titles and pull request titles alike, so one glance at any of the three tells you what kind of change it is. Format: <type>[optional scope]: <description>, where the scope is an optional noun naming the part of the codebase touched and the description is imperative, lower case, with no trailing period.

nodes.label: Git workflow reference
nodes.rationale: Every change travels the same path: a branch, small commits, a pull request, a review, resolved conversations, a rebase merge and a deleted branch. Nothing reaches main any other way.

nodes.label: Atomic commits
nodes.rationale: One reason to change per commit, and every commit builds on its own; a subject that needs the word 'and' is two commits.

nodes.label: Branch naming (<type>/<short-description>)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the commit types but is not machine-checked; it is a courtesy to whoever reads the branch list.

nodes.label: Breaking change marker (! and BREAKING CHANGE footer)
nodes.norm_label: breaking change marker (! and breaking change footer)
nodes.rationale: A breaking change takes a ! before the colon and explains itself in the body or in a BREAKING CHANGE: footer.

nodes.label: gh pr create --fill-first
nodes.rationale: --fill takes the title from the branch name on a branch with more than one commit, which the title check rejects. --fill-first takes it from the first commit, which may not describe the whole branch, so pass --title when it does not.

nodes.label: Conventional issue and pull request titles
nodes.norm_label: conventional issue and pull request titles
nodes.rationale: An issue describes the change as though committing it. Neither title becomes a commit subject, because rebase merges land the commits as written and discard the pull request title; the title is linted anyway because the pull request list, the notification and the reviewer see it first.

nodes.label: Merge rules kept by convention (branch rulesets and protection unavailable)
nodes.norm_label: merge rules kept by convention (branch rulesets and protection unavailable)
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the enforcement table can stop a merge. On a private repository, branch rulesets and branch protection need GitHub Pro, Team or Enterprise, and the API returns 403 for this one, so review, resolved conversations and green checks before merging are kept by convention rather than enforced.

nodes.label: Rebase merge, never squash
nodes.rationale: Rebase is the only merge method, so commits land exactly as written and the atomic history survives where a squash would discard it. The branch is deleted after the merge.

nodes.label: Server-side repository setup (gh api merge settings)
nodes.norm_label: server-side repository setup (gh api merge settings)
nodes.rationale: Applied once through gh api by someone with admin on the repository: allow only rebase merges (squash and merge commits off), allow auto-merge, and delete branches on merge.

nodes.label: Branch-to-merge loop
nodes.rationale: Branch off an up-to-date main, commit small, push the branch, open a pull request, get one approval, resolve every conversation, then rebase merge and let the branch delete itself. Review reads the commit history as well as the diff, because the history is what lands.

nodes.label: Enforcement layers (What enforces what)
nodes.rationale: Hooks, workflows and templates each block one thing, but nothing in the table can stop a merge. The local hooks and the CI workflows share one rule set, commitlint.config.mjs, so they cannot drift apart; the hooks give fast feedback and the workflows are the part that cannot be skipped with --no-verify.
